intro: The edit icon shows a pencil resting over a square, meaning change what is here. Put it beside profile details, settings rows, comments and saved content, where clicking turns read-only text into a form or opens an editor. The square tells people the pencil acts on an existing item rather than starting a blank page.
meaning: Pencils have long stood for writing that can be rubbed out and changed, so the pencil icon suits edits better than a pen. Placing it over a square narrows the meaning to editing an existing item, a pattern common in mail and settings screens. A pencil alone can also act as a write icon for composing something new. It differs from the note, which holds written content, and from the settings gear, which changes how things behave.
uses: Profile page: a button beside the name and bio that switches the fields into editable inputs.
Comment thread: an edit action in the menu of your own comments, shown only to the author.
Mail app header: a compose button that opens a blank message window.
Checkout summary: a link next to the delivery address so people can correct it before paying.
tips: Show edit icons on hover for dense tables, but keep them visible on touch screens, where there is no hover state to reveal them.
Give each pencil a specific label, such as Edit address, so screen reader users know which of many edit buttons they are on.
After saving, return clearly to the read-only state; leaving the pencil highlighted makes people unsure whether changes were kept.

faq.q: What does the pencil icon mean?
faq.a: It means edit or write. Next to existing content, it lets you change it, such as a name, address or comment. In mail and notes apps, a pencil on its own usually means compose, starting a new message or note from scratch.

faq.q: Where should the edit icon go next to a field?
faq.a: Place it right after the value it edits, on the same line, or at the top right of a card that holds several fields. Keep the position the same across the product, so people learn where to look without reading every label on the page.
